key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer combines improved photovoltaic efficiency with graphene-enabled environmental protection.
engineering_relevance: The architecture offers a route to more efficient, ambient-stable Schottky solar cells on untextured silicon substrates.
method: Benchmark planar trilayer devices against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Use PEDOT:PSS for anti-reflection, moderate graphene p-doping, and conductivity enhancement.
Use graphene as a charge-transport interface and moisture barrier.
evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si, retaining approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 ambient-exposure days versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
watch_item: The reported 75-day ambient test does not establish long-term outdoor durability or manufacturing-scale barrier integrity.
paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
